page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m8.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8163 processor cores running at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture supports instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512f, AES, BMI2, and FMA. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tier of modern cloud compute options. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests register weak performance in the bottom 25% of tested servers, with scores of 1103.89 and 2906.98 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a significant drop-off for large, uncached blocks, falling into the bottom 10% at 19.83 GB/sec for read operations. Geekbench results further confirm this trend, with a single-core score of 915.0 and a multi-core score of 1993.0, both categorized in the bottom 10%.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.u0.c1m8.xlarge is its reliance on older Intel Xeon hardware, which limits computational throughput and memory speeds but offers a high density of RAM relative to compute resources. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that require a larger memory footprint without demanding high CPU performance. It is suited for lightweight database operations, caching layers like Redis, simple web serving, and memory-bound utility tasks that do not require high-speed local storage or GPU acceleration.
